newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norsk Hydro sees 1997 on par with 1996.
newsitem.headline: Norsk Hydro sees 1997 on par with 1996.

text.p: Chief Financial Officer Georg Stoermer at Norsk Hydro ASA said on Monday he expected 1997 net profits to be at the same level as in 1996.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) Stoermer said the outlook for the current year was difficult.
"It is difficult to be specific. I think the best guess is that it will not be all that different (from 1996)," Stoermer said.

"Particularly on the net profit level, because we have a high tax rate on petroleum, and petroleum earnings do not mean as much as earnings in the other areas in terms of the net effect. So I think the net effect is likely to be on the same level as we saw in 1996."
Norsk Hydro posted operating profits down 10 percent at 9.65 billion crowns for 1996 compared with 10.70 billion crowns a year ago.

Net profits of 6.20 billion crowns, against 7.15 billion, included a reduction in the provision for deferred taxes of 776 million crowns due to a change in the tax law for hydroelectric power plants in Norway.
The company's share price fell heavily on the results and at 1240 GMT stood at 347.50 crowns, a drop of 31 crowns, or eight percent.
